question: Is the restored derivative drift repeatable with identical graph tensors, and is it sensitive to ATen CPU dispatch under otherwise fixed controls?

hypotheses.H_repeat: Independent instrumented processes reproduce prior restored outputs and each other exactly, including graph order.
hypotheses.H_graph: Graph/input arrays vary between equivalent control processes; stop if observed.
hypotheses.H_dispatch: Changing only ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY to default changes derivatives at fixed graph/weights/input; this can demonstrate kernel-dispatch sensitivity but cannot identify historical baseline hardware.

conditions.change: none; original one-thread restoration controls with capture-only hooks
fresh process, same D1 controls; negative repeat control
only ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY=default before Python starts; require observable capability differs from control

conditions.conditional: Only if D3 changes finite output at identical graph/weights; confirm generic result in fresh process

decision_rules: Stop if source/model/input/config/preserved manifests mismatch or other active calculation appears

D1 and D2 only initially. Require equal graph/input/weight hashes and exact output repeat; require D1 matches original restored output. Otherwise retain and stop with localized nonrepeatability or instrumentation/runtime confound.
If controls pass, run D3; no graph modification or alternate graph evaluation is warranted because current fast/legacy arrays are identical

If D3 has no output change, stop: selected dispatch contrast negative and historical cause not identifiable. If D3 changes output at same graph/weights, run D4 once; report sensitivity and repeatability without inferring historical hardware.

Stop on nonfinite output, timeout, exception, inaccessible included access/limit warning, four evaluations, 600 seconds cumulative calculation process wall time, or 1800 seconds investigation wall time from 2026-10-23T18:35:41Z. No retries of failed calculations.
additional_comparisons: Report all signed arrays, maximum absolute differences, exact equality, finite checks and unchanged acceptance for each condition against both historical baselines and restored result; repeat pairs and dispatch pairs compared too. Alternative condition success never retroactively changes failed restoration.
capture: eight graph tensors and byte hashes/dtype/shape
raw model output tensors and ASE energy/force/stress
effective in-process torch/backend/thread/affinity flags and whitelisted thread environment
limitations: Historical CPU/backend/graph data absent. Current measurements cannot fill historical fields.
Post-run probes are separate from effective in-calculation captures.
Float32 model; diagnostic only, no DFT/stability/synthesis/novelty/application evidence.
